newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU agrees extra E.Europe cattle imports.
newsitem.headline: EU agrees extra E.Europe cattle imports.

text.p: The European Union has agreed to import 500,000 head of cattle from eastern Europe at preferential tariff rates in 1997, EU officials said on Friday.
The move is intended to avoid any disruption of preferential access to the EU market pending the entry into force of the new arrangements, officials said.
Italy has been pressing for an increase in the quota from 425,OOO head as part of a series of measures to take account of the EU's expansion to include Sweden, Finland and Austria.
The EU grants special market access under a series of so- called Europe trade and cooperation agreements with prospective eastern European countries applying to join the 15-nation bloc.
The Commission said it will monitor the market for veal, calves and young cattle for fattening and take action if the imports undermine domestic prices.
This assurance is intended to defuse German and French opposition to increasing cattle imports when beef demand has fallen due to the mad cow crisis.
The agreement was adopted without discussion at a meeting of EU ministers. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
